content.text:
**I would request changes before treating this work as complete.** I reviewed all 21 PRs, #206–#226, against `origin/dev` at `7c6ec5122351`. The per-function separation is correct, and all 14 new DocsFn sites build. However, there are broken consumer examples, shared navigation defects, and substantial gaps in the requested documentation refresh.

1. **[P2] Existing sites still document APIs that no longer exist.**

   These are pre-existing inaccuracies left unresolved by work explicitly intended to bring those sites up to date.

   | PR | Verified remaining problem |
   |---|---|
   | **#207 AuthFn** | The [Next.js quickstart](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/8e142c2c8d7a8dbc762b07a2e4f760b0d118eef1/authfn/docs/content/docs/quickstart/nextjs.md#L64-L74) imports nonexistent `toNext`. Current exports provide `toNextHandlers`. SvelteKit guides similarly use nonexistent `toSvelteKit`; another guide imports nonexistent `toNextSession`. |
   | **#214 FileFn** | [Getting started](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/0dd2cbcb3361a607b0a9493318e12ea0ac99a276/filefn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L31-L38) imports `createLocalStorageAdapter` from `@superfunctions/storage`; it belongs to `@superfunctions/storage-local`. This repeats across framework quickstarts. Database guides also reference nonexistent `applySchemaToAdapter`, and processor examples use obsolete options. |
   | **#211 DataFn** | The [plugin example](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/4f34c1bc46afc0c1830385c119594fac8f088427/datafn/docs/content/docs/reference/events.mdx#L60-L85) supplies a `hooks` array. Current `DatafnPlugin` requires `runsOn` and named callbacks such as `beforeMutation`; it has no `hooks` property. |
   | **#223 SearchFn** | The [Hono quickstart](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/ff280cff49c21de47a2c2fa5a023723b008294e3/searchfn/docs/content/docs/quickstart/hono.mdx#L27-L47) calls `sf.adapter.initialize`, but the server exposes only `router` and `close`. It also passes a plain object where the router expects a Web `Request`. Similar patterns remain in other TypeScript quickstarts. |

   Adding administration pages or refreshing Python guides does not complete the existing-site refresh while these primary consumer paths remain broken.

2. **[P2] The shared new-site template has broken mobile navigation and missing search.**

   At a 390px viewport, tapping **Menu** opens the backdrop and sets `aria-expanded=true`, but the drawer remains `display:none` with zero dimensions. The imported DocsFn theme hides the sidebar below 1024px, and the open state never restores its display.

   Desktop testing also found no search trigger or dialog; keyboard shortcuts did nothing after hydration. The integration is in [the shared layout](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/7f6d58a01cc9292a9df822e2019062644417c15a/apifn/docs/src/routes/+layout.svelte#L17-L31).

   I reproduced these on ApiFn. All 14 new sites copy the same relevant template, styles, and dependency pins, so the correction needs to cover that entire group.

3. **[P2] McpFn’s quickstart is not import-safe or usable by its manifest tooling — #218.**

   The [example](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/fb63627965d95af2772465292dc835b8a86cfea7/mcpfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L45-L55) exports a named `declaration` and starts stdio at module scope, immediately before claiming the declaration is safe to import.

   The CLI loader consumes the default export or module itself. Running the documented example through `mcpfn manifest` reproduced **`Unsupported McpFn manifest formatVersion`**. Default-export the declaration from an import-safe module and put `serveStdio()` in a separate entrypoint.

4. **[P2] MemoryFn’s MCP example closes the server immediately after starting it — #220.**

   The [example’s `finally` block](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/5adfb40aa5ba628e392d0b21f4fe3802bb21867b/memoryfn/docs/content/docs/mcp.md#L18-L23) closes both the adapter and memory after `await adapter.start()`.

   `start()` resolves when the transport connects; it does not wait for the server’s lifetime. Consequently, this example immediately shuts down the service it just exposed. Cleanup should run when the host shuts down.

5. **[P2] SendFn’s Express mounting example imports a nonexistent function — #225.**

   The [reference](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/b6bcdf8253b37a35d7889f20285a343b5b0ec23a/sendfn/docs/content/docs/reference/typescript.md#L100-L104) imports `createExpressApp` from `@superfunctions/http-express`. That package exports `toExpress`, not an application factory.

   Consumers need to construct an Express application and mount `toExpress(client.router)`. The supplied example cannot compile.

6. **[P2] DevFn’s getting-started sequence never writes the configuration it subsequently loads — #212.**

   The [command sequence](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/b84bae1bb33e27220c1eab26184717ea1b50deba/devfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L8-L16) runs `init`, then `doctor --trust`.

   Without `--yes`, `init` only returns a preview with `written:false`. A fresh consumer therefore reaches `doctor` without a manifest. Include the explicit review-and-accept step, `init --yes`, before continuing.

7. **[P2] SearchFn’s FastAPI example exposes its captured handler as a request parameter — #223.**

   In the [route registration example](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/ff280cff49c21de47a2c2fa5a023723b008294e3/searchfn/docs/content/docs/quickstart/fastapi.mdx#L20-L31), `_handler=handler` appears in the endpoint signature. FastAPI interprets it as a query parameter.

   I reproduced a successful normal request becoming **HTTP 500** with `?_handler=test`, because the code then calls a string. OpenAPI also exposes `_handler`. Capture the handler through a factory closure, outside the endpoint signature.

8. **[P2] CliFn’s Commander example fails typechecking and does not propagate the action’s exit status — #210.**

   The [callback](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/c5b7f17db7cd64c3e032b291c7a1abaf6eccac74/clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/core-readme.md#L124-L136) returns `runAction()`, producing `Promise<number>`. Commander requires `void | Promise<void>`; a focused compilation with Commander 12 reproduced TS2345.

   Await the result, assign the returned status to `process.exitCode`, and show the asynchronous parsing entrypoint.

9. **[P2] Several new sites are outlines rather than comprehensive consumer documentation.**

   Concrete examples:

   - **#219 MDFN:** 38 pages contain only one code example. The [React reference](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/4affc4c9dbb4d5eb2385e3999d15b04bf662f851/mdfn/docs/content/docs/reference/react.md#L6-L10) is a short description without imports, component usage, or props. The framework guide redirects readers to repository examples instead of teaching installation and mounting.
   - **#216 LangFn:** [Models and providers](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/9d1d3332748ca3692eeabfb339a75c53c9ede976/langfn/docs/content/docs/models-and-providers.md#L8-L12) lists capabilities and links source exports, but never demonstrates constructing a real provider.
   - **#221 PlugFn:** [Connections and OAuth](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/b975ed8b01eeadebf6412f2ce9a5988dd31884d9/plugfn/docs/content/docs/connections-and-oauth.md#L8-L12) and workflow documentation describe capabilities without executable connection, action, or workflow examples.

   These need complete consumer journeys with setup, invocation, expected results, and failure handling.

10. **[P3] ReviewFn documents the wrong evidence directory — #222.**

    [Getting started](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/f944b66d411b9bb0c067830bb258e0b4e45ffe4a/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L17) says evidence is stored under `.reviewfn/artifacts`. The CLI writes retained evidence under the output directory, defaulting to **`.reviewfn/output/artifacts`**.

The desktop presentation is clean and consistent, but the mobile/search failures materially reduce its usability. From a maintenance perspective, copying the same 501-line server runtime into 14 sites also makes fixes expensive. Each layout additionally serializes the complete manifest and search artifact; audited responses reached roughly 878 KB uncompressed. A shared runtime and smaller client payload would improve this implementation.

**Validation and limits:** all 21 diffs passed whitespace checks; all 14 new sites built in isolation; 293 route requests returned successful responses or expected redirects. I traced examples against current source and ran focused compiler, CLI, FastAPI, and browser reproductions. UIFN’s generated-content check passed; its broader static verifier reported failures in unchanged files. Standalone DocsFn validation was blocked by missing built SearchFn dependencies in the isolated setup. I did not establish deployment readiness or clean builds for all seven existing sites.

The initial hosted-check snapshot contained failures; a final status refresh hit GitHub’s API rate limit. Git verification nevertheless confirmed all 21 reviewed heads remained unchanged. Your worktree and index were preserved, and I posted no GitHub reviews or comments.

write('adapters/db.md','''---
title: DB adapters
description: Configure the shared database adapter and provision FileFn tables.
---

# DB adapters

FileFn accepts `Adapter` from `@superfunctions/db`. Use `memoryAdapter` for disposable local state or `drizzleAdapter` for PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite.

```ts
import { memoryAdapter } from "@superfunctions/db/adapters/memory";
const db = memoryAdapter();
```

The published entrypoints are `@superfunctions/db/adapters/memory` and `@superfunctions/db/adapters/drizzle`. There are no separate `@superfunctions/db-postgres`, `db-sqlite`, or `db-drizzle` packages in this source tree.

## Schema and migrations

```ts
import { getSchema } from "@filefn/server";
const { version, schemas } = getSchema({ namespace: "filefn" });
console.log(version, schemas.map((table) => table.modelName));
```

This returns seven table descriptors, including fields and indexes. It does not provision a database. Translate/review these descriptors in your host's migration tooling and apply the migration before serving FileFn requests. The Drizzle adapter reports `schema.migrations: false`; it does not implement automatic DDL. Keep the namespace used in your migrations and `createFileFn` identical.

FileFn wraps the supplied adapter with its schema internally. For a custom adapter, implement the exported `Adapter` type rather than a positional CRUD interface: methods receive objects such as `findOne({ model, where })` and `create({ model, data })`. Respect the adapter's transaction and constraint capabilities; pretending to support transactions can break consistency guarantees.

See [Drizzle](./db-drizzle), [PostgreSQL](./db-postgres), [SQLite](./db-sqlite), and the [schema reference](../reference/schema).
''')
write('adapters/db-drizzle.md','''---
title: Drizzle DB adapter
description: Use the shared Drizzle adapter with PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite.
---

# Drizzle DB adapter

```sh
npm install @superfunctions/db drizzle-orm pg
```

```ts
import { Pool } from "pg";
import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/node-postgres";
import { drizzleAdapter } from "@superfunctions/db/adapters/drizzle";

const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL });
const db = drizzleAdapter({ db: drizzle(pool), dialect: "postgres" });
// Pass db to createFileFn({ db, storage, ... }).
```

Use dialect `postgres`, `mysql`, or `sqlite` with the corresponding Drizzle driver. The host owns the connection lifecycle; close the pool during application shutdown.

## Provision tables first

Use `getSchema({ namespace })` from `@filefn/server` as the source of table/field/index descriptors. Generate and review your host migrations, then apply them before running FileFn. Constructing the adapter or FileFn does not create SQL tables. The adapter does not expose an `applySchemaToAdapter` helper or automatic migration support.

See [DB adapters](./db) for the schema contract and [SQLite](./db-sqlite) for a local SQL configuration.
''')
write('adapters/db-postgres.md','''---
title: PostgreSQL adapter
description: Connect FileFn to PostgreSQL through Drizzle and pg.
---

# PostgreSQL

```sh
npm install @superfunctions/db drizzle-orm pg
```

```ts
import { Pool } from "pg";
import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/node-postgres";
import { drizzleAdapter } from "@superfunctions/db/adapters/drizzle";

const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL, max: 10 });
const db = drizzleAdapter({ db: drizzle(pool), dialect: "postgres" });
```

Pass `db` to `createFileFn`. Size the pool for your database connection budget and number of application replicas; `max: 10` above is an example, not a throughput guarantee. Call `pool.end()` during shutdown.

Provision the table and index definitions from `getSchema({ namespace })` through your host migration system before handling requests. Neither the adapter nor FileFn runs DDL automatically. There is no `generateSqlForSchema` export from a `@superfunctions/db-postgres` package. See [DB adapters](./db) and [schema](../reference/schema).
''')
write('adapters/db-sqlite.md','''---
title: SQLite adapter
description: Connect FileFn to SQLite through Drizzle.
---

# SQLite

```sh
npm install @superfunctions/db drizzle-orm better-sqlite3
npm install --save-dev @types/better-sqlite3
```

```ts
import Database from "better-sqlite3";
import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/better-sqlite3";
import { drizzleAdapter } from "@superfunctions/db/adapters/drizzle";

const sqlite = new Database("filefn.sqlite");
sqlite.pragma("journal_mode = WAL");
const db = drizzleAdapter({ db: drizzle(sqlite), dialect: "sqlite" });
```

Provision the FileFn tables from `getSchema({ namespace })` using the host migration system before serving traffic. Pass `db` to `createFileFn` and close `sqlite` during application shutdown. On Bun, use Bun's SQLite driver and `drizzle-orm/bun-sqlite` with the same `drizzleAdapter` entrypoint and dialect.

SQLite concurrency and filesystem durability depend on deployment topology. Use a database supported by your hosting environment; a local file is not shared storage across application replicas. See [DB adapters](./db).
''')

title: In-memory DB adapter

# In-memory database

```ts
import { memoryAdapter } from "@superfunctions/db/adapters/memory";
const db = memoryAdapter();
```
